item.title: Butterfly Effect in Kinetic Plasma Turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2611.33357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The butterfly effect is a fundamental process in chaotic systems, but it has not previously been characterized in detail for a collisionless turbulent plasma. In this work, we apply particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of driven turbulence to study the emergence of the butterfly effect from a small initial perturbation to the simulated particles. In particular, we compare pairs of (baseline and perturbed) simulations that differ only by a localized initial perturbation (down to the single-particle level). We find that the effect of the localized perturbation spreads radially throughout the PIC simulation, causing a difference between each simulation pair that is exponentially amplified over time within the affected region. The fields, including the electric current density, eventually become statistically decorrelated. We construct an analytical model combining spatial expansion with exponential amplification to approximate the early-time evolution. Varying the initial perturbation primarily affects the early-time evolution, while having little effect on the final, decorrelated state. We describe parameter scans with varying plasma beta and temperature (covering sub-relativistic and ultra-relativistic regimes). Our results show that remarkably small perturbations will grow to decorrelate each pair of simulations within a few dynamical times; the imposed perturbation can no longer be resolved once it falls below the numerical precision floor set by the machine precision. These results confirm that the butterfly effect is very strong and robust in a collisionless plasma, with implications for the predictability of turbulent plasma systems.
item.dc:creator: Louis Henderson, Vladimir Zhdankin

item.title: Global self-organisation via driven interchange turbulence in a hard-core Z-pinch
item.description: arXiv:2611.33618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whereas most magnetic-confinement concepts seek to suppress turbulent transport, the levitated dipole exploits it, with plasma turbulently self-organising to concentrate into the stronger-field region near the levitating coil. In a sufficiently large device, this can create the conditions needed for fusion, despite stiff and vigorous transport. We study this process in global simulations of a driven hard-core Z-pinch using compressible ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) with self-consistent evolution of the magnetic field. The results reveal how plasma and field jointly settle onto a continuously turbulent, finite-beta interchange-marginal family. Across a wide drive scan in two-dimensional simulations, quasi-universal pressure and density profiles result, with the magnetic-field profile changing from a decreasing vacuum-like form to one with an interior minimum at increasing beta. These profiles are robust to large changes to the heat and particle sources (including moving both to the outside of the device) as well as to different exhaust and boundary prescriptions. A designer consequently has little direct control over the selected profiles, including the final separation between the pressure maximum and coil, which is set by a turbulent boundary layer. We show that such results persist in the presence of three-dimensional fluctuations at modest beta, but that high-beta states become unstable to a field-parallel m=1 instability that is the analogue of the ballooning instability in a true dipole; this evacuates the core, destroying confinement. Based on a near-marginal expansion and a geometrical remapping, we argue that many features of our results should apply to any shearless closed-field-line system.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Squire, Christopher Hill, Laoisa Huckle

item.title: Speckle renewal, not bandwidth alone, mitigates kinetic Raman scattering at moderate bandwidth
item.description: arXiv:2611.33971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband lasers are expected to mitigate laser--plasma instabilities by shortening the coherence time. Using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of kinetic Raman scattering, we compare two broadband beams with identical power spectra but different speckle dynamics. At 2% bandwidth, where Brillouin scattering is negligible, induced spatial incoherence (ISI) gives 34% less Raman backscatter than a broadband beam focused through a random phase plate (RPP+BB), an ordering that persists with immobile ions. The two fields differ in their finite-time speckle contrast.
item.dc:creator: P. -E Masson-Laborde (CEA, LMCE), G Bouchard (CEA, LMCE), R Capdessus (CEA, LMCE), C Ruyer (CEA, LMCE), A Debayle (CEA, LMCE), A Fusaro (CEA, LMCE)

item.title: Formation of Electron Velocity Distribution Functions at low-\{beta} Quasi-Perpendicular Shocks From Physical-Mass-Ratio PIC Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.33989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At low-\{beta} quasi-perpendicular shocks, the origins of upstream field-aligned electron beams and downstream flat-top distributions remain unresolved. Using 2D fully kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations at the physical ion-to-electron mass ratio (mi/me = 1836), we found that the shock transition region is dominated by electromagnetic whistler-mode turbulence driven by the modified two-stream instability (MTSI) of reflected ions, not by the electrostatic instabilities as suggested by some previous studies using a reduced mass ratio. Beams in the upstream are produced mainly by shock-drift acceleration (SDA) at the ramp, whereas we attribute the downstream flat-top distributions to nonuniform acceleration by the parallel electric field. Electrons experience different field strengths, polarities, and interaction durations along their trajectories, leading to a spread of parallel velocity changes that broadens and flattens the distribution. These results highlight the importance of using the physical mass ratio in exploring the electron dynamics of low-\{beta} shocks.
item.dc:creator: Zhoufan Mu, Yao Chen, Hao Ning, Shan Wang, Sibo Xu, Terry Zixu Liu, Ao Guo, Hui Zhang, Hui Zhu

item.title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2611.34459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.
item.dc:creator: Matt E. Caplan, Evan B. Bauer, Mohammed Bettioua

item.title: A 2D fluid model in BOUT++/Hermes-3 for simulating detached divertor plasmas in tokamaks
item.description: arXiv:2611.34717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detached divertor operation is essential for controlling target heat fluxes in future high-power tokamaks. We present a two-dimensional fluid model implemented in BOUT++/Hermes-3 for simulating detached divertor plasmas with plasma-neutral interactions and fixed-fraction impurity radiation. We report improvements to the PETSc SNES-based steady-state solver used for two-dimensional axisymmetric transport simulations with fluid neutrals and assess the performance of several sparse-solver preconditioning strategies. For the cases considered here, STRUMPACK used as an ILU preconditioner with low-rank compression provides the most favorable performance, reducing the linear-to-nonlinear iteration ratio and achieving approximately a fivefold speedup relative to \HYPRE{}-based configurations. The optimized solver is then applied to DIII-D shot $\#174287$ at 4000~ms to characterize detached divertor conditions. Cross-field transport coefficients are adjusted to reproduce upstream experimental profiles, and detachment is modeled using nitrogen fixed-fraction radiation. Steady-state particle and energy balances are evaluated by decomposing the density and pressure equations into their transport and source terms. In the outer divertor, electron energy losses are dominated by ionization and impurity radiation, while ion energy losses occur mainly through collisional transfer to electrons. An upstream separatrix density scan shows decreasing target electron temperature and a rollover of the integrated target ion saturation current at higher $n_{e,\mathrm{sep}}$ consistent with expected detachment trends. These developments establish a foundation for future multispecies simulations. Hermes-3 is publicly available on GitHub under the GPL-3 open-source license.
item.dc:creator: Malamas Tsagkaridis, Ben Dudson, Mike Kryjak, Nami Li, Xueqiao Xu

item.title: Plasma transport by carrier electrons: Nernst advection beyond the heat-flow analogy due to kinetic stress
item.description: arXiv:2611.34766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nernst advection of magnetic fields down temperature gradients is lowered by kinetic stress from the $\underline{\underline{f}}_2$ electron distribution harmonic, which allows fluxes to stream past one another without isotropizing their lateral momentum. The long-held tie between heat-flow and Nernst advection is disrupted. When the distance between electron collisions is comparable to the magnetic field length-scale $L_B$, the kinetic stress affects magnetic transport in plasmas otherwise regarded as classical. This is from carrier electrons being deflected back and forth over the course of their trajectory. The field structure Knudsen number is defined: $Kn_B=14.8\frac{\lambda_{ei}}{L_B}\frac{Z+0.40}{Z+4.86}$, with Nernst velocity halved by kinetic effects at $Kn_B=1$. The kinetic stress is relocalized by magnetization, following the relocalization of heat-flux. Righi-Leduc heat-flow is found to be similarly suppressed by kinetic stress. The linear results of this paper are found to faithfully represent the non-linear evolution of magnetic field at a heat-front, indicating that low-$Z$ plasmas throughout magnetized-HED are demagnetized more slowly than previously anticipated.
item.dc:creator: C. A. Walsh

item.title: Statistical analysis of crossing beam speckle fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.33483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on the statistical analysis of single beam speckles, this paper develops a statistical description of speckle fields formed by crossing laser beams. A formal definition of individual speckles and their domains allows us to quantify the effective size and abundance of speckles. For two crossing beams, the effective speckle size is derived from the local curvature of the intensity field, and the expected speckle abundance is found asymptotically with the Kac-Rice formula. Monte Carlo simulations of speckle abundance show excellent agreement with the theoretical abundance formula. The two beam speckle analysis is then applied to a symmetric quad beam configuration motivated by polarization smoothing and demonstrates that increasing the separation between beams reduces expected stimulated Brillouin scattering reflectivity from saturated speckles. The statistical model is then extended to an arbitrary number of beams using a coordinate free formulation to obtain the spectral density of laser driven electron density fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, Pierre A. Michel

item.title: Relaxed magnetohydrodynamics with cross-field flow
item.description: arXiv:2604.03545v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The phase-space Lagrangian model of Dewar et al. (Phys. Plasmas 27, 062507, 2020) provides a framework for incorporating cross-field flow into relaxed equilibria while retaining ideal magnetohydrodynamics force balance. Here, we characterize the steady-state solution space and identify a solvability condition that couples the prescribed constrained flow to the geometry through the metric tensor. Using this condition, we construct equilibria in slab, cylindrical, and toroidal geometries. In toroidal geometry, the cross-field flow strongly correlates with magnetic-island structure: varying the rotation frequency modifies the dominant Fourier harmonic of the radial component of the magnetic field and can drive a transition from a primary (m = 1) island to secondary (m = 2) islands. In slab and cylindrical geometries, flow parameters weakly affect island width but strongly modify equilibrium profiles.
item.dc:creator: Arash Tavassoli, Stuart R. Hudson, Zhisong Qu, Matthew Hole

item.title: Simulation of trapped non-neutral plasma dynamics with rotating wall compression
item.description: arXiv:2608.19841v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A spectral macroparticle simulation scheme is used to model non-neutral plasma dynamics in a Penning-Malmberg trap. This grid-free numerical scheme is well adapted to the specific geometry of trapped plasmas, with varying longitudinal and transverse profiles in a cylindrical conducting pipe. The cutoff spectral harmonics provide control over the trade-off between accuracy and noise smoothing, which is especially important in the three-dimensional case. We demonstrate the ability of this scheme to obtain the dispersion relation of the plasma modes from the inherent simulation noise, providing a valuable tool for understanding the plasma's behavior. In the presence of a rotating wall drive, we show that the numerical scheme can reproduce the time evolution of the driven eigenmodes, identify the limit of the linear response with increasing drive amplitude and retrieve the compression rate dependency on the drive frequency, known from the weak drive regime of the rotating wall technique. Since the model contains no cooling, drive-induced heating restricts the simulations to short times and the weak-drive regime. To the authors' knowledge, such simulations have not been reported in the literature so far.
item.dc:creator: Luisa Riik, Oliver Boine-Frankenheim

item.title: Demonstration of H-mode Error Field Identification in a Single Discharge via Island Healing
item.description: arXiv:2609.30452v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-disruptive compass scan error field identification via island healing is demonstrated on KSTAR in a single H-mode discharge. This method can allow for up to a 75% reduction in the operational time necessary for a complete compass scan by reducing the required discharges from four to one. Previous experiments on DIII-D, JET, and MAST-U have demonstrated the technique in Ohmic and L-mode but required multiple discharges and high fidelity real time n = 1 magnetic diagnostics located close to the plasma, which are unlikely to be viable for future devices. The results presented here were made possible by implementing a new set of triggering algorithms relevant to fusion pilot plant operation into the KSTAR plasma control system, along with KSTAR's strong RMPs and long pulse lengths. This represents a significant step towards the disruption-free error field identification method being demonstrated for deployment on future disruption-averse tokamaks, including ITER and fusion pilot plants. Steps needed to close remaining gaps to viability are addressed.
item.dc:creator: E. M. Bursch, A. Xie, J. L. Barr, S. K. Kim, N. C. Logan, S. M. Yang, J. G. Bak, W. Choi, Q. Hu, J. W. Juhn, J. Kim, J. Lee, N. Leuthold, J. K. Park, C. Paz-Soldan, L. Piron, G. Seo, J. Seo

item.title: Plasma transport by carrier electrons: delocalization length for heat-flux
item.description: arXiv:2610.32085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The kinetic understanding of the three magnetized heat-flux components is unified in the linear regime with a full electron-electron collision operator and a converged harmonic expansion of the electron distribution (up to $f_6$). The delocalization length $\lambda_d=\lambda_{ei} Z/\sqrt{Z+4.45}$ is an improved heat-flux non-locality metric accounting for the localizing effect of electron-electron collisions on the electron population carrying heat-flux. Magnetization also localizes the carrier electrons; the delocalization Hall parameter $\psi_d=13.4 \chi Z/(Z+4.45)$ shows that this occurs at a faster rate than magnetization of thermal conductivity ($\psi_{\kappa}= 9.94\chi(Z+0.17)/(Z+5.88)$). The traditional Knudsen number, which uses the electron-ion mean-free path, does not fairly represent non-locality across ionization and magnetization; $Kn_d = 8.28\lambda_{d\bot}/L_T$ should instead be used. Righi-Leduc suppression is found to be the square of the perpendicular suppression, with no additional length-scale required. This approach lays the groundwork for consistent treatment of kinetic plasma transport, with subsequent papers addressing the kinetically-modified induction equation.
item.dc:creator: C. A. Walsh

item.title: Multi-pump amplification of frequency-separated Stokes waves in stimulated Brillouin side scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.15293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin side scattering (SBSS) can be enhanced when one side-scattered light wave is amplified by several pump waves through different ion-acoustic waves (IAWs). This mechanism differs from models in which several pumps share the same scattered-light wave or the same IAW. Side-scattered light generated by different pumps can propagate in nearly the same direction but have different frequencies. We examine this process using a local temporal-growth calculation, a finite-width Gaussian k-space model, a three-dimensional envelope model, and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These cross-beam three-wave interactions increase temporal growth and convective gain over the crossing angles considered. In the three-dimensional envelope calculations, direct SBS interactions alone produce weak, localized side scattering, whereas including the cross-beam interactions produces a strong response for the same incident fields and initial perturbations. The enhancement remains when the total incident power is fixed, so it comes from the cross-beam interactions rather than from extra laser power. The PIC simulations show stronger side scattering and several pump-specific IAWs, with a non-monotonic dependence on beam number. These results identify cross-beam amplification of frequency-separated side-scattered light as a gain pathway that should be considered when interpreting multibeam SBS experiments.
item.dc:creator: Y. Chen, Qing Wang, H. Wen, Y. X. Li, S. Tan, C. Y. Zheng, Z. J. Liu, L. H. Cao, C. Z. Xiao
